purpose: Test whether row-specific L11H3 downstream margin readers collapse to a stable direction-level operational reader that transfers leave-one-row-out across syntax and nouns.
data_status: RETROSPECTIVE_FROZEN_CAUSAL_LATTICE; gradients and reader-transfer predictions are new; diagnostic requiring prospective promotion if it passes

binding_parent.finding: One row-specific central reader prospectively predicts 512 amplitudes, including 448 unopened intermediates.

novelty_audit: Searches for direction-shared reader, leave-one-row-out downstream gradient, and shared margin-reader transfer found no prior authority event.
This is operational reader grouping across examples, not a low-rank fit or activation reconstruction.
map: Recompute one target-free central margin gradient g_i per row exactly as in the sealed full-lattice test. For each row i, average g_j over all other rows with the same answer direction and predict all sixteen q_i(S) by g_LOO,direction dot delta_h_i(S). Compare only afterward with the frozen complete causal lattice. A global leave-one-row-out gradient is the matched sharing control; the already-validated row-specific reader is the upper benchmark.

predictions.pred_a_gradient_instrument: All source/downstream closures <=5e-5 and all 32 central gradients are finite and nonzero.
predictions.pred_b_direction_reader_transfers: Across 512 amplitudes, direction-LOO cosine >=0.95, relative L2 error <=0.35, and sign agreement >=0.90.
predictions.pred_c_reader_transfers_each_template: Each template separately has cosine >=0.90, relative L2 error <=0.45, and sign agreement >=0.85.
predictions.pred_d_reader_transfers_intermediate_com: The 448 intermediate amplitudes have cosine >=0.95, relative L2 error <=0.35, and sign agreement >=0.90.
predictions.pred_e_direction_grouping_beats_global: Direction-LOO reduces squared error at least 20% versus global-LOO, demonstrating that answer direction is a necessary grouping variable.
predictions.pred_f_reader_geometry_is_stable: Minimum row-gradient cosine with its direction-LOO reader is >=0.80.

null: Failure of b-d means the reader remains row/context-specific. Failure of e means one global reader is equally adequate. Failure of f means any task prediction is driven by displacement geometry despite unstable reader identity. No rank or post-outcome fitted reader is permitted.
